purpose: Replace mistaken dolphin identity with existing gray shark; rebuild original mouth anatomy.

arguments.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw Image 1, the exact original SLEVEJM2 001 sprite, as one polished cartoon SHARK sprite. Image 1 controls pose, mouth shape, facing, visible anatomy, framing and water occlusion. Images 2 and 3 are CHARACTER DESIGN AND DRAWING STYLE ONLY, not pose. Match the established shark: neutral medium gray skin, pale ivory jaw and underside, gill slits, bold black outlines, smooth restrained cel shading, heavy sly brows and razor-sharp triangular teeth. This is the sneaky shark character, never a friendly dolphin; no dolphin beak or rounded dolphin teeth. Pose: Shark rears up diagonally toward upper-right in a right-facing rear three-quarter view, showing mostly gray back/flank, narrow pale underside. The upper head is high and compact; a small eye sits high on it, with a toothed mouth opening and a hint of reddish mouth interior below. The exaggerated projecting lower jaw reaches far toward upper-right in the original, forming the bottom of the mouth, not a dolphin beak. Keep the original backward dorsal fin extending lower-left and near pectoral fin hanging vertically against the body. Retain the diagonal body lean and exact visible cropped waterline. Preserve the source silhouette and relative positions while replacing pixel steps with smooth ink. Only the character parts above water are drawn, with a thin cyan-and-white ripple at original cutoff. Do not complete submerged body, tail or legs. One character only. All contours inside canvas with clear transparent padding on every edge. Actual transparent RGBA background, no checkerboard, scene, cast shadow, glow, text or collage.
